digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### OpenAI frontier models and Codex are now available on AWS
URL: https://openai.com/index/openai-frontier-models-and-codex-are-now-available-on-aws/
OpenAI breaks its Azure exclusivity, signaling a strategic pivot toward distribution breadth over platform lock-in.
This is a significant shift in OpenAI's cloud strategy. By expanding to AWS, OpenAI gains access to AWS's dominant enterprise customer base while reducing dependency on Microsoft's infrastructure. For enterprises already committed to AWS, this removes a major friction point for GPT adoption and puts pressure on Anthropic's AWS-first positioning.

### Nvidia chases $200B CPU market with AI agent PCs from Microsoft, Dell, and HP
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/nvidia-chases-200b-cpu-market-with-ai-agent-pcs-from-microsoft-dell-and-hp/
Nvidia moves downstream from data center GPUs into consumer silicon, targeting Intel and AMD's core market.
The $200B CPU TAM represents Nvidia's next growth vector as data center GPU sales mature. Partnering with Microsoft, Dell, and HP on "AI agent PCs" suggests a new device category where local inference becomes the selling point. If agents require always-on local compute, this could fundamentally reshape PC refresh cycles and margin structures.

### CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
URL: https://cs336.stanford.edu/
Stanford open-sources a complete LLM training curriculum, democratizing foundation model development.
This is infrastructure for the next generation of AI talent. When elite institutions publish full training pipelines, it compresses the knowledge gap between frontier labs and well-funded startups. Watch for a proliferation of specialized models from smaller teams who can now skip years of trial-and-error on training fundamentals.


## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### Anthropic files to go public
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/anthropic-files-to-go-public/
The AI lab race to public markets begins, setting a valuation benchmark for the entire sector.
Anthropic's IPO filing is the first true test of public market appetite for pure-play foundation model companies. Their enterprise traction will face scrutiny against their compute burn rate. This filing gives us the first audited look at unit economics in frontier AI and will directly inform OpenAI's own IPO timeline and Alphabet's AI competitive positioning.

### Alphabet plans to raise $80B to pay for AI buildout
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/alphabet-plans-to-raise-80-billion-to-pay-for-ai-buildout/
Google's parent signals AI demand is outstripping even Big Tech's balance sheet capacity.
An $80B raise from a company with Alphabet's cash generation is extraordinary. The filing language—"demand exceeding available supply"—suggests they're losing deals due to capacity constraints, not product gaps. This is a capex arms race signal: infrastructure spend across hyperscalers will remain elevated through 2027 minimum, benefiting Nvidia, TSMC, and power/cooling infrastructure plays.

### Defense tech darling Mach Industries hits $1.8B valuation, a 4x jump in a year
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/defense-tech-darling-mach-industries-hits-1-8b-valuation-a-4x-jump-in-a-year/
A 22-year-old founder commands $1.8B for autonomous defense vehicles, reflecting DoD's urgency to modernize.
$300M at 4x year-over-year valuation growth with five autonomous vehicles in development and a completed acquisition. Mach's trajectory mirrors Anduril's early days but compressed. The defense tech sector is seeing venture returns that rival commercial AI, with longer contract durations and stickier revenue. Thornton's age is irrelevant; the execution velocity is the signal.

### Water access is now a risk factor in SpaceX's IPO
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/water-access-is-now-a-risk-factor-in-spacexs-ipo/
SpaceX's S-1 reveals data center cooling as a material constraint on their AI infrastructure ambitions.
This disclosure confirms SpaceX is building significant compute infrastructure beyond Starlink operations. Water scarcity as a stated risk factor suggests they're competing for the same constrained resources as hyperscalers. Geographic arbitrage for water access may become as important as power cost in data center siting decisions.


## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Hackers hijacked Instagram accounts by tricking Meta AI support chatbot into granting access
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/hackers-hijacked-instagram-accounts-by-tricking-meta-ai-support-chatbot-into-granting-access/
Meta's AI customer support was social-engineered into facilitating account takeovers at scale.
This is the first major case of AI agents becoming the attack surface rather than the defense layer. Meta deployed AI support to cut costs; adversaries found it more manipulable than human agents. Every company racing to automate customer service with LLMs should treat this as a case study in why agent permissions require zero-trust architectures and human-in-loop for sensitive actions.

### Florida sues OpenAI, Sam Altman, in first-of-its-kind lawsuit over violent incidents
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/01/florida-sues-openai-sam-altman-in-first-of-its-kind-lawsuit-over-violent-incidents/
A state government attempts to establish AI company liability for downstream user actions.
The Florida State University shooting connection makes this legally novel—state AG is arguing product liability extends to AI outputs. If this theory survives early motions, it creates regulatory uncertainty that could slow enterprise adoption and force AI companies to implement more aggressive content filtering. Watch for Section 230 intersection arguments and insurance market response.

### Launch HN: Expanse (YC P26) – Unlock Wasted GPU Capacity
URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48356312
YC-backed startup tackles GPU utilization arbitrage as compute costs remain the primary AI bottleneck.
The pitch targets stranded GPU capacity—machines provisioned but underutilized. If Expanse can aggregate fragmented compute into reliable capacity, they're building infrastructure that benefits from the Alphabet-style demand overflow. The timing aligns with enterprises discovering their reserved capacity sits idle while inference demand spikes unpredictably.


## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The capital concentration is staggering: Alphabet raising $80B, Anthropic going public, Mach at $1.8B, Gigascale's $250M climate fund—all announced in a single news cycle. The infrastructure layer is where conviction capital is flowing, from GPUs to water rights to distributed compute arbitrage. Meanwhile, Meta's chatbot hack and Florida's lawsuit reveal the governance and liability frameworks lagging badly behind deployment velocity. The next 18 months will be defined by who can scale infrastructure while managing novel attack surfaces and regulatory exposure.
